articles.title: Trump claims US is ‘looking into’ Iranian bomb plot in Washington despite ‘no credible threats’
articles.summary:
US officials ‘continue to debate whether Iran can or will attempt to execute’ plot to detonate a ‘dirty bomb’, report says

Donald Trump has claimed the US is “looking into” whether Iran is…

blocks.text: Donald Trump has claimed the US is “looking into” whether Iran is developing plans to detonate a so-called “dirty bomb” in Washington, even as the White House said there are “no credible threats” at this time.
Trump said his administration takes the idea “very seriously”

After a CNN report, citing seven unnamed US officials, that new US intelligence suggested Iran was working on plans that would use a dirty bomb, which combines conventional explosives with radioactive material, or a chemical weapon against senior Trump administration officials.
The report noted, however, that US officials “continue to debate whether Iran can or will attempt to execute such a plot”.

The US president’s war on Iran is deeply unpopular among Americans. His Republican party was widely rejected by voters in the midterm elections, in which the GOP lost control of the Senate and House of Representatives.

Asked in the Philippines on Tuesday if there was reason to believe that such an Iranian attack was imminent, Trump said: “If there is, they will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before. I hope it’s not, but we take it very seriously because they happen to ​be crazy.”
Lauren Bis, a White House spokesperson, said in a statement: “We remain vigilant monitoring any and all potential threats, but at this time there are no credible threats to the homeland.”

CNN cited the unnamed officials as saying that Tehran’s planning was an effort by Iran to “give itself options rather than an indicator of an imminent attack”, but the plans include specific locations and targets.
While the plans would signify that Iran is willing to escalate its tactics against the US, there is no evidence to suggest they will go ahead with them.

The US and Israel went to war with Iran starting in February, with early airstrikes killing Iranian officials, including supreme leader Ali Khamenei. Trump has repeatedly claimed the war will be over soon, but it has continued.

The US president has argued that US involvement in the war is necessary so that the country doesn’t build nuclear weapons. Iran has blocked trade through the strait of Hormuz, creating rising fuel costs – and rattling the global economy.

articles.title: ASEAN leaders, 8 dialogue partners commit to UNCLOS
articles.summary: Leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations and eight dialogue-partners adopted last night a joint declaration of their strong commitment to international law, particularly the United…

blocks.text: November 18, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and eight dialogue-partners adopted last night a joint declaration of their strong commitment to international law, particularly the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).

In their declaration – adopted during the 21st East Asia Summit (EAS) in Manila – the ASEAN and its eight dialogue-partners reaffirmed their “shared commitment to maintaining and prompting peace, security and stability in the region, as well as to the peaceful resolution of disputes, without resorting to the threat or use of force, in accordance with international law.”
They called the UNCLOS the indispensable foundation of a more peaceful and prosperous world and freedom of navigation and overflight.
ASEAN’s eight dialogue partners are China, Australia, India, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, Russia and the United States.

The joint declaration was issued against a backdrop of China’s continued assertion of its expansive claim in the West Philippine Sea, and the hostile activities of its coast guard and navy against local fishermen and civilian vessels.
In their joint declaration, ASEAN and EAS leaders vowed to promote and uphold international law to ensure peaceful settlement of disputes.

They expressed commitment to advancing regional cooperation and promoting the sustainable use and management of marine resources as well as the protection of submarine cables, pipelines and other critical underwater infrastructure.
They also underscored the need for strong political will and international cooperation to affectively address online scams and strengthen the countries’ financial and digital systems.

The leaders expressed grave concern over the escalating threat posed by transnational criminal organizations inflicting harm through online scams, including those originating from scam centers, and associated human trafficking that can have a severe impact on people in vulnerable situations.
The leaders acknowledged the exploitation of digital and other advanced technologies and digital financial platforms by increasingly sophisticated criminal actors.
They also cited the need to strengthen financial and digital systems while acknowledging the severe human consequences associated with scam centers and related criminal activities.

articles.title: Lacson questions VP camp’s ‘honest mistake’ claim
articles.summary: Sen. Panfilo Lacson yesterday cast doubt that Vice President made an “honest mistake” in declaring shares in GenCorp Industries in her statement of assets, liabilities and net worth.

blocks.text: November 18, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Panfilo Lacson yesterday cast doubt that Vice President made an “honest mistake” in declaring shares in GenCorp Industries in her statement of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALN).
Lacson was reacting to former chief presidential legal counsel Salvador Panelo, who made the remark in defense of the Vice President.
On X, Lacson tweeted that the Vice President’s “honest mistake” in declaring GenCorp shares despite its absence in the incorporation papers is a “double-edged sword.”

“Its meaning depends on the state of mind and intent of the person behind it. It can be an inadvertent slip that exposes the truth, or a genuine blind spot that mistakes falsehood for reality. Ultimately, only the person responsible can say which is which,” he added.

The Senate impeachment court is looking at the impeachment article on Duterte’s alleged unexplained and hidden wealth and for having business interests despite a constitutional ban during a Vice President’s tenure.
GenCorp is declared in her SALN as among the firms where the Vice President had shares. However, GenCorp’s corporate records did not identify her as an officer or shareholder.

Another allegation against the Vice President was her receipt from 2022 to 2025 of up to P2.14 million in “return of capital” or earnings from her “loose investment” of just P46,875 at a Jollibee branch in Davao City.
Meanwhile, an impeachment verdict may come as early as December if the defense completes its remaining eight to 10 witnesses within the next few weeks, the prosecution said.

House prosecutor and Bicol Saro party-list Rep. Terry Ridon said the defense could finish presenting its evidence by the end of November or during the first week of December, if they only have around eight to 10 witnesses to present. — Daphne Galvez

articles.title: Panelo links threats to VP’s ex-staff to government
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte’s camp believes that the alleged threats made against a former member of her household staff could be linked to the Marcos administration.

blocks.text: November 18, 2026 | 12:00am
MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte’s camp believes that the alleged threats made against a former member of her household staff could be linked to the Marcos administration.
Duterte spokesman Paolo Panelo issued a statement yesterday and disclosed that at 11:19 p.m. on Monday, the Vice President received a text message from her former staff.

“The message contained a desperate plea for help and rescue in Manila. The sender claimed to be in the custody or under the control of certain individuals who allegedly told them about a threat to their lives,” he said.
The message sender alleged that they were being forced to sign a document but they refused.

“We are deeply concerned that this incident may be part of what we believe to be a relentless campaign by the Marcos administration, utilizing state institutions like the NBI (National Bureau of Investigation), against the Vice President,” Panelo added.
He mentioned similarities with the incident concerning Jefry Tupas, the former chief information officer of Davao City when the Vice President was still city mayor.
On Sept. 29, NBI agents allegedly told Tupas that there were threats to his life and attempted to bring him to Manila.
Panelo said at the time he wrote the statement, they had no idea of the whereabouts of the former household staff, and have yet to independently verify the staff’s safety and well-being.

He explained that they brought the incident to the public and media’s attention because of the alleged “unremitting efforts of the government to harass, threaten and coerce individuals into becoming false witnesses in support of trumped-up charges against VP Sara Duterte, weaponize state agencies and undermine the rule of law for political ends.”
“The safety and liberty of this former staff member must be guaranteed without delay,” Panelo added.
Palace: Fake news
Asked to react to Panelo’s statement, Palace press officer Claire Castro said the Marcos administration is not in the business of sowing intrigue and fabricating evidence.

“Creating intrigue and planting evidence are not being done at present, things that the Duterte administration was used to doing and this was admitted by former president Duterte before the media,” she said.
“There is no room for fake news under the present administration,” said Castro.
However, Castro said the claim should be investigated to determine if it is true.
PNP: File report
The Philippine National Police urged the Vice President’s camp to come forward with the information that her former household staff is being held against their will by a group of people.
PNP spokesman Brig. Gen. Allen Rae Co said Duterte or any representative has yet to file a formal report to the police.
“The trigger that will start our investigation is if they will formally or at least personally report it to us, not through social media,” he said at a news briefing.
Co assured Duterte they are ready to assist in efforts to locate her former household staff, stressing the PNP is always ready to protect anyone regardless of political affiliations.
The NBI also urged Duterte to file a formal report, saying it cannot investigate claims circulating only on social media.

NBI Director Melvin Matibag said yesterday the bureau had received no formal complaint or referral regarding the reported incident, despite what he described as coordinated social media posts about the alleged disappearance of the Vice President’s former staff members. — Alexis Romero, Emmanuel Tupas, Mark Ernest Villeza

articles.title: Major issues on Code of Conduct settled – Marcos
articles.summary: Although a binding code of conduct for South China Sea claimants was not completed under the Philippines’ chairship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, President Marcos said the…

blocks.text: November 18, 2026 | 12:00am
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. speaks during a press briefing at the International Media Center in Pasay City on November 17, 2026
Ryan Baldemor / The Philippine STAR

MANILA, Philippines — Although a binding code of conduct for South China Sea claimants was not completed under the Philippines’ chairship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), President Marcos said the major issues surrounding the proposed rules have been settled.

At a media briefing after the ASEAN Summit closing ceremony, Marcos quoted Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro as saying that 85 to 90 percent of the code of conduct “has actually been done.”

“We had, of course, hoped that during the chairship of the Philippines, that we would be able to announce that the COC (code of conduct) was finished. However, that’s not the case,” the President told reporters at the International Media Center in Pasay.
“But we can take solace in the fact that the majority of the issues – actually, the large issues – are already done and decided and agreed upon,” he added.
Marcos said negotiators still have to thresh out the definition of terms to make the code comprehensible to all parties.

“There are definitions, and there are phrases, and there are paragraphs that need to be clearly defined, so that it is very understandable, and it is very clear to everyone involved that these are the rules, these are the understood and accepted mores and norms that we will all be following,” the Chief Executive said.
Marcos thanked the ASEAN members and China for their participation in crafting the binding code of conduct, saying “everyone has worked hard to bring us to the point that we are in now.”

He said there was a tacit agreement that the parties would abide by the Declaration on the Conduct of Parties in the South China Sea (DOC), a non-binding document adopted in 2002 to prevent tensions in the strategic sea lane. “Until the COC is ready, until it is finalized, until it is signed by all parties – by ASEAN, by China – then we pledge to continue to follow on the DOC’s guidance,” Marcos said.

“ASEAN and China reaffirmed firm commitments to sustaining the effort, towards the conclusion of the final phase of negotiations, or a substantive and effective COC, consistent with UNCLOS (United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea), and it effectively will govern the behavior of parties at sea,” he added.

articles.title: China to ASEAN: Promote peace, trust despite tensions
articles.summary: Pointing out that “flame runs high when everyone adds wood to the fire,” a ranking Chinese official yesterday called on the Association of Southeast Asian Nations to promote peace and…

blocks.text: November 18, 2026 | 12:00am
President Marcos joins hands with other ASEAN leaders plus South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae and Chinese Premier Li Qiang on November 17, 2026.
PPA Pool

MANILA, Philippines — Pointing out that “flame runs high when everyone adds wood to the fire,” a ranking Chinese official yesterday called on the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) to promote peace and mutual trust as tensions over the the South China Sea simmer.

Chinese Minister of Agriculture and Rural Affairs Zhang Zhu cited the need for parties to “fend off risks and challenges together,” accelerate regional integration and “inject more positive energy to stability and prosperity” in the region and beyond.

“The more difficulties we face, the more unity and coordination we need. The foundation of cooperation is mutual trust,” Zhang said during the 29th ASEAN-Plus Three Summit. ASEAN-Plus comprises the members of the regional bloc as well as Japan, South Korea and China.

“Countries in the region should do more things that would contribute to mutual trust and regional peace and stability. Shoulder more sense of responsibility other than geopolitical calculations. Only in this way can we harness the role of ASEAN-Plus Three cooperation as a main channel of East Asian cooperation,” he added.

Zhang made the remark as Filipino and Chinese officials engage in ugly public exchanges over Beijing’s illegal claim over the West Philippine Sea, the part of the South China Sea within the Philippines’ 200-nautical mile exclusive economic zone and continental shelf.
Philippine officials have denounced Chinese acts of provocations at sea, but Beijing dismissed the allegations as exaggerations.
China claims virtually the entire South China Sea, which serves as the passageway to more than 60 percent of global trade.
The other claimants are Taiwan and ASEAN members Vietnam, Malaysia and Brunei.
ASEAN and China signed a non-legally binding Declaration on the Conduct of Parties in the South China Sea in 2002 to prevent tensions from escalating and maintain stability in the region.

However, legally binding rules have yet to be completed and approved. Officials have admitted that the code of conduct would not be finished within the period of Philippines’ hosting of the ASEAN Summit this year.
In 2016, an arbitral tribunal based in The Hague invalidated China’s wide-reaching maritime claim, but the Chinese government refused to recognize the landmark decision.
In his opening remarks for the ASEAN-Plus Three Summit, President Marcos called for joint efforts to ensure that existing commitments would be felt by citizens.

“As we approach 30 years of ASEAN-Plus Three cooperation, let us renew our ambition for this partnership and shorten the distance between the commitments we make around this table and the benefits our peoples feel in their daily lives,” he added.

articles.title: Japan PM wants Asia oil security task force created
articles.summary: Japan proposed yesterday the creation of the Asia oil security task force that would coordinate cooperation on oil stockpiling and release of supplies during emergencies as countries seek to mitigate…

blocks.text: November 18, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Japan proposed yesterday the creation of the Asia oil security task force that would coordinate cooperation on oil stockpiling and release of supplies during emergencies as countries seek to mitigate the impacts of oil supply disruptions stemming from the Middle East crisis.

Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae introduced the initiative at the 4th Asia Zero-Emission Community (AZEC) leaders’ meeting during the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in Pasay City.
“I also wish to propose an initiative for cooperation on oil stockpiling in Asia through the use of idle tanks in Japan,” Takaichi, who chaired the AZEC with President Marcos, said in her remarks.
The Asia oil security task force will be Asia’s equivalent to the International Energy Agency (IEA), the Japanese leader said.
Established in 1974 following the oil crisis in 1973, IEA requires member-countries to stockpile oil equivalent to 90 days of consumption.
Takaichi said the initiative would be coordinated with the Philippines-led joint stockpiling scheme.
She called for the strengthening of the Partnership on Wide Energy and Resources Resilience (POWERR) Asia, announced this year, evolving the existing AZEC into AZEC 2.0.
Takaichi also proposed the “POWERR Gulf Initiative,” which aims to strengthen coordination between oil-producing countries and energy-consuming countries in Asia.
“Japan will serve as the nexus connecting oil-producing countries in Asia,” she said.
Marcos, for his part, said disruptions along critical supply routes, such as the Strait of Hormuz, “never stay local.”
“They reverberate across global supply chains. As I emphasized at the AZEC Plus Online Summit, no single nation can insulate itself from shocks of this magnitude by acting alone,” he said.
Marcos said the Philippines was making progress on its strategic petroleum reserve and is seeking investments in energy projects to achieve regional energy security.
“But stockpiling is not enough. Sustainable and enduring energy security demands that oil consuming and oil producing nations act in unison,” he said.
“We must deepen information sharing and practical storage arrangements, as well as commit to upholding international law to keep sea lanes open and maintain fair, transparent markets,” Marcos said.
He proposed a regional study on joint oil stockpiling to strengthen energy security at the AZEC Plus online summit in April.
AZEC is a Japan-led initiative aimed at promoting clean energy, reducing carbon emissions and supporting sustainable economic growth while strengthening energy security across the region.
AZEC members include Japan, the Philippines, Australia, Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.

“Under this POWERR Asia initiative, we are going to provide assistance to construct for example to stockpile, providing facilities of crude oil, or support, provide capacity, building assistance, or share the expertise in order to establish system of a stockpiling, not only the facility itself, but also the system as a whole,” Japanese Foreign Ministry Press Secretary Toshihiro Kitamura told journalists at a separate press briefing.
AI safety
Takaichi also launched the Japan-ASEAN Artificial Intelligence (AI) Safety and Security Partnership to respond to emerging risks of cybersecurity threats and loss of human control over AI.
The Japan-ASEAN AI Safety and Security Partnership is part of efforts to expand the Japan-ASEAN Co-Creation Initiative for AI.

“As a trusted partner of ASEAN, Japan will support ASEAN member-states to build AI safety governance capabilities suited to their national circumstances, thereby co-creating a safe, secure and trustworthy AI ecosystem and enhancing its resilience, through the following lines of efforts,” the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan said in a statement.
The partnership will be implemented in coordination with the ASEAN Working Group on AI Governance and the ASEAN AI Safety Network. — Pia Lee-Brago

articles.title: BINI, SB19 earn first Grammy nods
articles.summary: P-pop groups BINI and SB19 earned their first Grammy nominations, while Filipino-American artists Bruno Mars and Olivia Rodrigo bagged nods in the top categories of the 2027 Grammy Awards.

blocks.text: November 18, 2026 | 12:00am

P-pop royalties BINI and SB19 have made history as the first Filipino groups to receive Grammy nominations. BINI’s ‘Unang Kilig’ and SB19’s ‘Visa’ are among the six nominees in the newly introduced Best Asian Pop Music Performance category at the 69th Grammy Awards scheduled for Feb. 7, 2027.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — P-pop groups BINI and SB19 earned their first Grammy nominations, while Filipino-American artists Bruno Mars and Olivia Rodrigo bagged nods in the top categories of the 2027 Grammy Awards.
During the nomination announcement held Monday evening, BINI’s “Unang Kilig” and SB19’s “Visa” were among the songs included in the inaugural Best Asian Pop Music Performance category.

After exploring genres, BINI went back to their bubblegum roots with “Unang Kilig,” written and produced by Jeremy G, which talks about the feeling of uncertainty and excitement in the first stages of romance.
“A historic moment for OPM (Original Pilipino Music), for Filipino music and for everyone who believes in them,” BINI said in a post.
“The girls are making history, and we couldn’t be prouder! Thank you to everyone who continues to support us,” they added.

On the other hand, Visa, written by Pablo and produced along with his brother Joshua Daniel Nase, draws inspiration from the group’s experience of the obstacles they have to just get their visa and perform abroad.
“From the Philippines to the world, thank you for believing in SB19 and standing with us as we carry Filipino music to the global stage!” SB19 said in a post.
As the agency’s ambassadors, the Department of Tourism (DOT) congratulated both groups’ new feats on the global stage.

“From rocking the historic stages of ‘Coachella’ and ‘Lollapalooza’ to earning recognition on the world’s biggest music stage, our country’s tourism ambassadors continue to prove that P-pop is a global force to be reckoned with,” the DOT said.
“The world is listening, and Filipino music is shining brighter than ever!” it added.

Other nominees in the Best Asian Pop Music Performance category include Sunset Kiss by the Japanese group Babymetal featuring Polyphia, Yes by Japanese singer Lisa and K-pop songs 404 (New Era) by KiiiKii and Bang Bang by Ive.

The Recording Academy said the Best Asian Pop Music Performance award aims to honor “artistic excellence in Asian pop music performances originating from or widely recognized within Asian markets, including but not limited to K-pop, J-pop and C-pop.”
However, the category drew flak from several music critics, stressing that it is boxing Asian acts instead of recognizing them alongside other global artists.

The criticism echoed when K-pop boy group BTS announced that they would not submit in this year’s awarding ceremony with their supposed comeback album “Arirang” after all of their members completed their mandatory military service.
Meanwhile, Filipino-American artists Olivia Rodrigo and Bruno Mars swept the pop and general field categories, making them some of the most nominated artists in this year’s awarding ceremony.
Bruno’s The Romantic and Olivia’s You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love bagged the Album of the Year and Best Pop Vocal Album nominations.
Olivia’s The Cure was nominated in both Record of the Year, Song of the Year and Best Pop Solo Performance.

articles.title: Marcos hails ‘successful’ Philippines chairship of ASEAN
articles.summary: President Marcos turned over the chairship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations to Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and described the Philippines’ hosting of the bi-annual…

blocks.text: November 18, 2026 | 12:00am
President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. hands over the ceremonial wooden gavel to Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, marking the transfer of the ASEAN chairmanship on November 17, 2026.
Presidential Communications Office / Facebook page

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos turned over the chairship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations to Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and described the Philippines’ hosting of the bi-annual meeting of the 11-member regional bloc as “successful.”
Marcos also called on leaders to ensure that ASEAN’s progress would continue to be felt by its people.
In his speech during the closing ceremony, Marcos said the Philippines’ chairship would be remembered not only for what leaders decided upon, “but for what ASEAN is now better able to do.”

“The ASEAN takes prominence in summits such as these, but it must be brought to life every day across our region by ministers, by officials, negotiators and experts, businesses and civil society, young people, communities and by the countless people who work quietly behind the scenes to give meaning to our ambitions and to make our work of real consequence,” he said.

“I am so happy that we were able to bring that team together, and that they worked so well together that we were in the end able to do what we have to achieve and what we have succeeded to do in this ASEAN. So I think it is a success,” Marcos said at a press conference at the International Media Center.
The President cited the important outcomes of the three-day summit, including the signing of the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement.
Marcos expressed support for Singapore’s ASEAN’s chairship next year.
He is confident that Singapore would lead “with a clarity of purpose, steadiness and commitment to regional cooperation for which it is known and for which these times demand.”
“The most important work of ASEAN cannot belong to one chair alone. Progress endures when each chair builds on what came before and leaves stronger foundations for what comes next,” he said.

For his part, Wong said 2026 has been a challenging year for the region and the world, but “ASEAN has remained united and continued to move forward with ambition and purpose” under the leadership of the Philippines.
Aside from the leaders from ASEAN and dialogue partners, also present at the closing were former president and now Pampanga Rep. Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo and other government officials.

Among those who performed during the closing ceremony at the Philippine International Convention Center in Pasay City were singer-songwriter Gary Valenciano and SB19, who performed “Together in Motion,” the official theme song of the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits.
SB19 is a tourism ambassador for the Philippines.
Leaders and guests cheered when Timor-Leste Prime Minister Kay Rala Xanana Gusmao danced with the performers.
Timor Leste will chair the ASEAN in 2029.

articles.title: Charges loom for 114 erring gas stations
articles.summary: The Department of Energy is preparing to take legal action against 114 gas stations that failed to comply with last week’s major fuel price rollback.

blocks.text: November 18, 2026 | 12:00am
Motorists queue at a gasoline station in Marikina on July 27, 2026.
Walter Bollozos / The Philippine STAR
MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Energy (DOE) is preparing to take legal action against 114 gas stations that failed to comply with last week’s major fuel price rollback.
The DOE’s field offices inspected 213 gas stations from Nov. 10 to 13, the week the agency ordered players to cut gasoline prices by a whopping P16.80 per liter.

“Unfortunately, 114 were found not to have implemented exactly what was mandated,” DOE-Oil Industry Management Bureau director Rino Abad said at a virtual press conference yesterday. “Instead of P16, they cut prices at only P10 or P12.”
The DOE did not specify where the non-compliant gas stations were located.
With the Philippines still under a national energy emergency, the DOE has the authority to dictate price adjustments under the Downstream Oil Industry Deregulation Law.
Abad also cited Presidential Decree 1865, signed in 1983, which involves petroleum products and national security.
Those found guilty of violating the decree may be imprisoned for two to five years and fined between P20,000 and P50,000.
“Based on the discussions with our legal department, these two laws can be used for their assessment and appreciation in case these inspections turn into actual cases,” Abad said.

articles.title: Quad vows to ensure open maritime corridors
articles.summary: Leaders of Australia, India, Japan and the United States criticized what they described as “destabilizing or unilateral actions” affecting regional peace and stability, in a meeting held…

blocks.text: November 18, 2026 | 12:00am

At the Quad summit held in Manila, Philippines on the 17th, from left to right: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, U.S. President Donald Trump, and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese pose for a commemorative photo.
AFP / Yonhap

MANILA, Philippines — Leaders of Australia, India, Japan and the United States criticized what they described as “destabilizing or unilateral actions” affecting regional peace and stability, in a meeting held on the sidelines of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in Manila.
US President Donald Trump arrived yesterday and met with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae.
The countries, constituting the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad), said their group is “a force for good and a partnership of action, committed to peace, stability and prosperity.”

“We strongly oppose any destabilizing or unilateral actions that seek to change the status quo, including by force or coercion, which escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and stability. We express grave concerns about economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions,” they said in a joint statement.
“We commit to work together to ensure open, safe and resilient maritime transit corridors in the Indo-Pacific.”

Quad also vowed to secure critical supply chains, protect freedom of navigation and overflight, drive growth through technologies of the future, including investments and deployment of trusted artificial intelligence (AI), and respond to disasters with life-saving assistance.

“We commit to work together to ensure open, safe and resilient maritime transit corridors in the Indo-Pacific. We are working with regional partners to tackle shared challenges and drive opportunities to deliver tangible benefits to the Indo-Pacific,” the group said.

The Quad meeting took place days before Trump’s trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China on the sidelines of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation meet.

China, whose aggressive actions in the resource-rich South China Sea has drawn widespread condemnation, had accused Quad of trying to sow enmity between Beijing and its neighbors and disrupting regional peace.

In the same statement, the four leaders also announced the inaugural Quad Business Leaders’ Forum to be held next year. The event aims to bring together business leaders, government officials and policy experts from Quad countries to foster greater business ties across private sectors.
The Quad leaders also affirmed the importance of the AI Accelerator, announced by their foreign ministers in Atlanta.
“The Accelerator is intended to coordinate and fund efforts to support trusted AI access, deployment and technical assistance across the Indo-Pacific,” they said.
The group also welcomed the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration, a new initiative that seeks to enhance information sharing and maritime domain awareness.
It also acknowledged the “rapid increase” in the number and scale of cyber incidents in the region and announced an enhanced Quad Cybersecurity Cooperation to achieve an open and secure cyberspace.

“We unequivocally condemn terrorism and violent extremism in all its forms and manifestations, including cross-border terrorism, and commit to strengthening the Quad’s ongoing cooperation on counterterrorism,” Quad added.
The four countries also reaffirmed their “unwavering” support for ASEAN centrality and unity and committed to uphold a free and open Indo-Pacific.

articles.title: Rights court rules Turkey must release jailed lawmaker Atalay
articles.summary: The European Court of Human Rights has called for the release of imprisoned elected lawmaker Can Atalay. Atalay has been in prison for almost five years despite rulings from the Turkish…

image.caption: Can Atalay's party, TIP, has long been calling for his releaseImage: ANKA

blocks.text: The European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) ruled against Turkey over the detention of human rights lawyer and elected lawmaker Can Atalay.
The ECHR published its decision on Tuesday, saying that Turkey must release Atalay and allow him to take up his seat in the Turkish parliament.
The court ruled that his continued detention had been intended to silence him and undermine political pluralism.
It ordered Turkey to pay him €32,500 (about $35,700) in compensation.
The judges stressed that Atalay's case should not be considered separately, but rather in the wider context of the detention of political opponents, human rights activists and journalists in Turkey.
No future in Turkey? Growing exodus of young Turks

Turkey was among the original signatories of the European Convention on Human Rights. Yet it has previously refused to comply with the court's decisions in the cases of rights activist Osman Kavala and prominent Kurdish politician Selahattin Demirtas.
From leading activist to a jailed member of parliament
As a lawyer, Atalay represented victims in numerous social and political cases in Turkey, as well as in freedom of speech cases involving journalists and writers.
He was also among the leading voices in the 2013 Gezi protests, which the government called an attempted coup.
Because of his involvement in the protests, Atalay, along with seven others, was sentenced to 18 years in prison in April 2022 for "aiding and abetting an attempted coup."
Continuing his struggle from the infamous Silivri prison, Atalay ran as a candidate for the Workers' Party of Turkey (TIP) in the 2023 parliamentary elections.
LGBTQ+ communities in Turkey fear intensifying clampdown
A candidate for the earthquake-hit province of Hatay, he won his seat but was denied release despite multiple rulings by the Constitutional Court, Turkey's top court.

His parliamentary status was revoked in 2024, a decision the Constitutional Court later overturned. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's party stopped the opposition from formally reading the decision in parliament.
Although a year later an opposition lawmaker read the decision in parliament, Atalay remains in jail.
After the ECHR's ruling was published, TIP leader Erkan Bas took to social media to call for Atalay's release and the restoration of his parliamentary mandate.

articles.title: Fresh clashes at the Eritrean border — is Ethiopia sliding into a regional war?
articles.summary: As Ethiopian troops push Tigrayan forces toward the Eritrean border, fears of a new regional war are growing. With tensions rising between Ethiopia, Eritrea and Sudan, the Horn of Africa faces…

image.caption: Tensions in the Horn of Africa are at an all-time highImage: EDUARDO SOTERAS/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: After a few weeks of relative stability, fresh clashes in the contested Ethiopia-Eritrea border areahave raised fears of a full-fledged war. Meanwhile, diplomatic relations between Ethiopia and Sudanhave hit new lows.

Fighters allied with the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) launched their offensive on September 23. It was aimed at overthrowing the Ethiopian government as part of a larger rebel coalition. But the Ethiopian National Defense Forces (ENDF), backed by pro-government militia, have steadily pushed the TPLF out of Tigray, a region in northern Ethiopia.

According to the conflict tracker of the monitoring organization ACLED, the ENDF have pushed further into Tigray, effectively driving the Tigrayan Defense Forces (TDF) towards the border with Eritrea. Skirmishes have been reported from several locations, while the ENDF have fired heavy artillery towards dwellings close to the Eritrean border town of Badme.

While no census data is publicly available, Badme appears to be a small rural town on satellite images. However, the locality is historically significant for both sides because it was the ground zero of the Eritrean-Ethiopian War from 1998 to 2000, sometimes dubbed the Badme War.

The war ended with theAlgiers Agreement, in which both countries agreed to honor the rulings of a newly formed Eritrea-Ethiopia Boundary Commission. The commission awarded Badme to Eritrea, a decision that Ethiopia challenged at times. Abdurahman Sayed, director of the London-based Horn of Africa Center for Regional Integration, told DW that Ethiopia might see an advantage in reclaiming Badme to resolve its current internal struggles.
"It seems now if the Eritreans withdrew and the Ethiopians came back, it could be to calm down the Tigrayans, especially those who are now supporting the party in power in Ethiopia", Sayed said.
Ethiopia: Who is fighting whom — and why?

He suggested that people like Getachew Reda, a former spokesman for the TPLF and current advisor to Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, might be able to win the Tigrayan people over to side with the federal government through territorial gains for the Tigray region.
The ever-looming threat of a full-fledged war with Eritrea
"The coming of the forces to the Eritrean-Ethiopian border clearly indicates that the conflict can be triggered any time", Abdurahman Sayed said.

Eritrean and Ethiopian government troops allied against the Tigrayan forcesduring the 2020-22 Tigray conflict. Since then, Eritrea's allegiances have shifted towards the TPLF and away from Abiy Ahmed's central government. In October, the two neighbors cut diplomatic ties. At one point, Eritrean troops reportedly crossed the border into Tigray.
Ethiopia's broken Tigray peace deal opens old wounds

Magnus Taylor, a regional analyst with the International Crisis Group (ICG), believes that Addis Ababa's prime objective for the moment might rather be securing its northern border and destroying supply lines between Eritrea and Tigrayan forces.

"So what we might actually be seeing is a kind of a function of the attempts by the Ethiopian military to consolidate its control of Tigray, which includes pushing Tigray's borders with Eritrea", Taylor told DW.

However, securing control over Tigray could also involve direct conflict with Eritrea at one point, Taylor said: "If this happens, then it's quite likely that the Ethiopians would attempt to carry out all their objectives in Eritrea at one time."

Since Eritrea seceded from Ethiopia in 1993, Ethiopia has been the world's largest landlocked country by population. Prime Minister Abiy has repeatedly described the country's lack of sea access as an existential threat. While stating a preference for peaceful means to gain access, he said this could also mean capturing Eritrea's easternmost port, Assab, by force.

blocks.caption: The ongoing clashes have displaced many local residents like this Amhara woman to other parts of EthiopiaImage: Marco Simoncelli/AFP

blocks.text: Ethiopia-Sudan relations at crossroads
At the same time, the diplomatic relations between Ethiopia and its northwestern neighbor, Sudan, have deteriorated even further.

Sudan and Egypt, both downstream the river Nile, have been on edge for years because of Ethiopia's Grand Renaissance Dam (GERD). The massive GERD, built on the Blue Nile just kilometers from Ethiopia's border with Sudan, gives Addis Ababa significant leverage over the timing and regulation of water flows downstream, raising concerns in Sudan and Egypt over water security and dam operations. The Ethiopian government has rejected claims that the dam could be used as a means to pressure Sudan and Egypt.

blocks.caption: The RSF militants reportedly receive support from Ethiopia and the United Arab Emirates. However, both countries deny the allegationsImage: Rapid Support Forces/AFP

blocks.text: Since 2023, Sudan has been embroiled in a civil war between two rival military forces: the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), led by General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), led by Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti. In mid-November, both sides accused the other of direct participation in each other's internal conflicts.

Two countries with severe internal conflicts and mirroring alliances: Could the situation deteriorate further into potential direct fights between the two armies? ICG's Magnus Taylor believes there is a risk, but at least not for now.

"The most likely scenario is we just get a continuation of this kind of proxy style of involvement with each other's opposition groups rather than formal direct involvement on the ground in the conflict," Taylor said.
Sayed also believes that, at the moment, there is no need for direct confrontation.

"The RSF can do the job that Ethiopia and any other country backing them wants them to do," Sayed said. "But if there is a need and the RSF are failing, the Ethiopian army could be pushed to get involved."

articles.title: How the attack on Crimean Bridge unfolded
articles.summary: One of the key symbols of Russia's occupation of Ukraine has suffered major damage after a seven-stage attack by Kyiv.
articles.byline: Laura Gozzi, Ilya Abishev, Richard Irvine-Brown

blocks.text: The attack on the strategic Crimean Bridge was carried out gradually to cut across several layers of defence, Kyiv confirmed on Tuesday.
For several weeks Ukraine's Security Service and its General Staff phased out air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare assets, and other designated targets, President Volodymyr Zelensky said.

A significant strike had already been reported on 16 November, when drones hit the bridge at night. Traffic was paused briefly then reinstated, and although the arch over the road section was visibly damaged, the structure remained standing.
But that hit turned out to have been only the penultimate stage of a complex attack.
In the early hours of 17 November, the final strikes dealt a fatal blow to the weakened arch structure.

One verified video - filmed from a camera on board a Ukrainian-made Flamingo missile - shows the weapon approaching the main span of the bridge and heading towards the steel arches, with the footage freezing just before impact.

The Flamingo had potentially been modified to be controlled remotely, which improved its accuracy enough to strike the bridge supports, munitions expert Justin Bronk from the Royal United Services Institute said.
The missile's "very heavy warhead" made it "more suitable" for attacking the bridge's reinforced concrete spans and supports, Bronk added.

Zelensky later confirmed that several types of missiles and drones had been employed in the attack, which led the massive road arch - weighing thousands of tonnes and measuring about 227m in length - to collapse into the strait.
Daylight images taken from the shores of Crimea to the north show a section about 200m (660ft) long of the tarmac was too dragged below into the sea.

This is clearly critical damage to the crossing. Far from just being a decorative feature of the bridge, the arch played a structural role, transferring loads and supporting the span and helping to ensure the stability of the entire structure.

The parallel arch supporting the railway section has remained standing, although it may also have been damaged. All traffic on the bridge was initially suspended, though trains were later allowed to resume running.

But the damage to the bridge's main span is "catastrophic", Colin Capriani, a structural engineer from Monash University in Melbourne, Australia, told BBC Verify. It was "very hard to envisage" how the bridge could be rebuilt given it is clearly well within range of Ukrainian weaponry, Capriani added.
Major attacks in 2022 and 2023 had already caused serious damage to the road spans of the bridge, but the structure survived.

The difference this time is "the most critical and vulnerable part of the bridge has been hit", said David MacKenzie of engineering consultancy COWI, adding that "although the wreckage of the bridge can be cleared fairly quickly, reinstating full road traffic will take over a year".

Moscow uses Crimea as a military base, with airbases, troop concentrations, training grounds and artillery stockpiles. From there it also carries out strikes on the rest of the country and resupplies its troops in southern Ukraine.

The attack comes after a summer of frequent strikes on Crimea, dictated by Ukraine's stated goal of cutting the peninsula off from Russia. At the time, Kyiv vowed to turn the Crimean Peninsula "into an island".
Now - although it is too early to speak of a complete blockade of Crimea – the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis has increased significantly.

There is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of the Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions. However, Ukraine has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar, which has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo.

Moscow can also still utilise the ferry crossing across the Kerch Strait. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited - and anything on the Black Sea has become vulnerable to attack. Resupplying Crimea by sea is risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area.

In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge - particularly its enormous arch - may have blocked the shipping channel. This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for ports in the Sea of Azov, including the occupied cities of Mariupol and Berdyansk.
Away from the operational value of the damage to the bridge, the symbolic significance remains.
In 2018, Putin triumphantly drove over the bridge representing the unification of Russia and Crimea in a Russian-made truck. That section of the road now lays on the seabed.

Nearly five years since he launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Putin continues to wreak destruction on Ukraine's civilian population, but his most prized symbols of power are increasingly threatened by Kyiv's reach.

articles.title: Carney eyes 'other options' for embattled Canadian auto sector on China trip
articles.summary: The PM has suggested Chinese automakers could replace American ones in Canada - but some say that would not be easy.

blocks.text: Carney eyes 'other options' for embattled Canadian auto sector on China trip
ByNadine Yousif
Senior Canada reporter
The plight of Canada's car industry has become one of the clearest stress tests of Ottawa's effort to weather US tariffs and chart a path forward.

The past year and a half has been tough on the sector since US President Donald Trump imposed a 25% tariff on non-American-made vehicles, upending decades of free trade and automotive integration with Canada.
Now Prime Minister Mark Carney has signalled that he is looking to China, where he is on a visit for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit (Apec), as part of the solution.
But that avenue is not without controversy, and is once again drawing the ire of those close to Trump.

While in Cambodia earlier this week, Carney told reporters that Canada could turn to European and Asian carmakers to save its auto manufacturing sector if a trade deal with the US could not be reached.
"Look - great auto workers, important market, real assets in Canada," he said. "If they're not fully utilised in a North American context, that provides other opportunities.
"Canada's going to move forward either way."

He went on to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in China on Tuesday for their second head-to-head in less than a year. The two talked afterwards of the importance of developing their relations, and Carney said they had agreed to further tariff cuts.
Neither side mentioned vehicles specifically, though analysts suggest the issue will have been prominent in their minds.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Carney and Xi met on Tuesday to discuss cooperation and trade ahead of this week's Apec summit

blocks.text: Image source, Getty Images
Carney and Xi met on Tuesday to discuss cooperation and trade ahead of this week's Apec summit

In January, Carney said that opening the door to China's electric vehicles, external (EV) could result in investment into Canadian-owned companies and the creation of manufacturing jobs in the sector.
American tariffs on imports of Canadian-made vehicles have led to thousands of job losses in Canada and anxiety over the future, as 90% of cars made in Canada are shipped to and sold in the US.

At the same time, China has been eyeing Canada as a potential entry-point to the North American EV market. Earlier this year, Canada announced that it would let in 49,000 EVs from China at a low tariff rate, with plans to raise that quota gradually to 70,000 by 2030.
The move was a significant break from the US, which has tariffed Chinese EVs heavily since the presidency of Joe Biden to protect domestic manufacturing.
Chinese EV manufacturers like BYD and Chery have already been lobbying the Canadian government for access.

Last week, Canada's Minister of International Trade Maninder Sidhu toured a Chery plant in China, external to discuss their potential entry to the Canadian market. He told reporters afterwards that Canadians could expect to see affordable Chinese electric vehicles for sale in Canada by early 2027.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Canada's international trade minister Maninder Sidhu toured a Chinese EV plant earlier this month

blocks.text: Image source, Maninder Sidhu/X
Canada's international trade minister Maninder Sidhu toured a Chinese EV plant earlier this month
These moves come as the toll of US tariffs on Canada's auto sector has become harder to ignore.

Stellantis, an American car manufacturer that made models like the Dodge Challenger and the Chrysler 300 in Canada, recently announced it would sell its assembly plant in Brampton, Ontario - a move that Carney characterised as a "betrayal" of the plant's 2,200 workers.

The facility had been idle since 2023 for a planned retooling, but what was supposed to be a temporary shutdown became permanent after Trump's tariffs, leading the company to shift some manufacturing to Illinois in the US.
Stellantis said it would sell part of its Brampton plant to Roshel, a Canadian defence contractor and manufacturer of armoured vehicles.
The Canadian auto workers' union has expressed concern about the deal, calling it "underhanded" and warned that Canada would lose thousands of high-paying jobs as a result.

The deal has also led to speculation that a Chinese EV manufacturer could move into the facility, after Canadian media outlet CTV News reported, external, citing anonymous sources, that Stellantis was planning to lease back 25% of its plant to assemble "affordable" EVs.
There are prominent voices who oppose any such move, including within Canadian politics.
In a letter to Carney, Ontario Premier Doug Ford warned against opening the door for Chinese EV kits to be assembled in Canada at the Brampton plant.
China overwhelmingly builds its cars at home and ships them whole - or to be assembled in kits - overseas.

Lynette Ong, director of the China Governance Lab at the University of Toronto, said introducing Chinese auto manufacturing in Canada would be "controversial" due to fears that Canadian jobs could be lost and that the North American auto manufacturing industry could be eroded.
"We want to make sure they're hiring Canadian workers, that they are helping train Canadian workers and that they are transferring the technology over," Ong said.
She argued that Canada should also be wary of making itself vulnerable to potential security breaches and foreign interference from China, as well as risking the ire of the Trump administration.
That already appears to be happening. Peter Navarro, Trump's senior counsel for trade and manufacturing, warned Carney against cosying up to China in a post on X, external.
"Are u really threatening to play China off the U.S.? This is offensive in the extreme," he wrote on Monday. "You should be far more worried China is going to eat Canada alive."
His comments were reposted by Pete Hoekstra, the US ambassador to Canada.
Why China is winning the global EV race

Canadians' views of China have grown more positive since Trump's return to the White House. An Angus Reid poll released on Tuesday, external suggests many are open to Chinese investment in the EV sector, but with additional security or restrictions.

The Carney government has set terms for China's entry to Canada's auto market, including that any venture should be jointly-owned by a Canadian company, that it must follow Canadian labour standards and that the cars should be built using Canadian-made parts.

Ahead of his meeting with Xi on Tuesday, Carney also noted there are "clear guardrails" in how Canada deals with China, including barring work on sensitive matters like artificial intelligence and critical minerals.
Canada has also eyed other partnerships. It is notably pursuing associate member status with the EU, and had signed a free trade deal with the Philippines earlier this week.
Just how much Canada is willing to embrace Chinese manufacturing, however, still depends on the outcome of ongoing US-Canada trade talks.
Progress has been made in negotiations with the US, Carney recently said, but differences remain. It is unclear if Trump and Carney will speak on the sidelines of the Apec summit later this week.

articles.title: 49th ASEAN Summit closes, Philippines turns over chairmanship to Singapore
articles.summary: Watch the closing ceremony of the 49th ASEAN Summit here

blocks.text: Watch the closing ceremony of the 49th ASEAN Summit here

MANILA, Philippines – Leaders wrapped up the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and Related Summits with a closing ceremony at the Philippine International Convention Center in Pasay City on Tuesday, November 17.
Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. emphasized that challenges confronting Southeast Asian nations have become “increasingly intertwined,” as he delivered his closing remarks.

“Energy security is also economic security. Maritime stability sustains peace, trade, and livelihoods. Technology brings opportunity, but also new questions of security and governance, inclusion. And climate change knows no frontiers, testing the resilience of our communities,” Marcos said.
“Our institutions must therefore become as connected as the challenges that we face, and ultimately every member state must be able to count on ASEAN and ASEAN must be able to count on every member.”
During the ceremony, 2026 ASEAN chair Philippines also turned over chairmanship of the regional bloc for 2027 to Singapore.
“To Prime Minister [Lawrence] Wong and the people of Singapore, we have the utmost confidence. We offer our friendship and our full and complete support,” Marcos said.
In his remarks, Wong congratulated the Philippines “on a very successful ASEAN chairmanship,” and thanked Marcos “for steering ASEAN through a difficult year.”
Wong also announced that Singapore has chosen “Deeper Integration, Wider Partnerships” as the theme for its ASEAN chairmanship in 2027, the year the bloc turns 60.

“‘Deeper Integration,’ because we can do much more to realize the full potential of ASEAN. This includes strengthening our links in finance, digital technologies, and energy. We must take further steps toward a single ASEAN market, where businesses can set up and operate more seamlessly across borders, and where our people can enjoy more opportunities to work, invest, and prosper,” Wong said.

“‘Wider Partnerships,’ because ASEAN must continue to be open and and outward-looking. At a time when the world is becoming more divided, our response is to keep building bridges, to strengthen ties with our partners…and to ensure that Southeast Asia remains a region where all countries can engage and cooperate.”
The speeches were followed by musical performances from Julie Anne San Jose, Gary Valenciano, and P-pop group SB19.
Watch the closing ceremony in the video above. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Nvidia forms national security committee after Huang affair
articles.summary: Nvidia has created a board-level committee for national security and export control. This follows the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang over extramarital affairs, allegedly including one with a Chinese…

image.caption: The scandal and Huang's resignation have taken a hefty bite out of the share price of the world's most highly valued companyImage: CFOTO/picture alliance

blocks.text: Nvidia on Tuesday said it had created a board-level national security and export-control committee.

This follows the scandal surrounding former CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned last week over extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China and working to help ensure higher quality chips crucial to AI development made it to the Chinese market.

The events have heightened oversight of the US tech giant and its importance to national security, as well as wiping several hundred billion dollars off the stock market valuation of what investors treat as the world's most valuable company in the space of a month.

blocks.caption: Nvidia's celebrity CEO Jensen Huang, who liked to flaunt his relationship with Donald Trump, was forced to step down abruptly last weekImage: Soeren Stache/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: What are Nvidia's plans for the new oversight committee?
Nvidia is calling the new group its National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee.

Suzanne Nora Johnson, a former vice chair at Goldman Sachs, will chair the committee, joined by fellow directors Stephen Neal, a former CEO of a law firm, John Dabiri, a professor of aeronautics and mechanical engineering at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech).
The committee will meet at least once every quarter. It will also incorporate independent legal, national security and trade compliance experts.
Nvidia already has a lower-level National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team; these groups will report to the board-level committee.

"We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation," Board Chair Harvey Jones said in a statement.
The company did not explicitly link the decision to November's developments and Huang's rapid fall from grace, but the timing seemed conspicuous.
The decision was announced hours ahead of Nvidia publishing its third-quarter results, with its still-stratospheric share price having fallen roughly 28% in the past month.
Trump's ASEAN Play: The new front in the US-China chip war
How has the scandal highlighted the question of US-China chip trade?

US President Donald Trump, whom Huang was influential in persuading to allow the export of better-quality Nvidia chips to China than other US companies and officials deemed prudent, welcomed Nvidia's move on arrival in the Philippines on Tuesday.
"Yes, that's a good idea. It's a great company," he said during a photo opportunity at a Manila meeting with the other "Quad" leaders from Australia, India and Japan. "It's a great idea."
Trump reportedly owned Nvidia stock worth tens of millions of dollars before the share price fell. He also owns shares in other big tech companies.

Huang resigned last week after admitting to extramarital affairs in a message to Nvidia employees. This followed widespread reports, seemingly based on US and other intelligence, that one of the affairs was with a woman who used to lead a Singapore-based cloud computing company.

That company, Megaspseed International, is a major Nvidia client and is suspected of diverting advanced chips to China in violation of US export controls. Intelligence officials also suspect Huang's partner of being an asset of Chinese intelligence services.
The reporting on the case also seems to show these suspicions had been known to US officials and other countries, including Singapore, for roughly a year.

articles.title: ASEAN, US adopt principles to combat online scams --Marcos
articles.summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Tuesday announced that the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and the United States have adopted principles to combat online scams, along with a…

blocks.text: Published November 17, 2026 10:50pm

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Tuesday announced that the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and the United States have adopted principles to combat online scams, along with a statement outlining 10 principles for public-private partnerships to address the growing threat.
Marcos made the announcement during the ASEAN-US Special Summit in Manila, attended by US President Donald Trump and other ASEAN leaders.

The Philippine president described the adoption of the principles and the statement as an immediate and concrete outcome of the special summit, emphasizing the importance of delivering results beyond diplomatic discussions.

“In anticipation of your arrival, Mr. President, and knowing your desire for results and not just talk, our staffs have been working together, ASEAN and your staffs have been working together, and we have come to being able to finalize and have adopted the principles to tackle online scams,” Marcos said.
He added that the participating governments had also adopted “a statement on ten public-private partnership principles on tackling online scams and the comprehensive work plan.”
“And so that is an immediate result of this special summit between ASEAN and the United States,” he said.
The announcement highlights the importance of closer cooperation between governments and the private sector in addressing online scams, which have become a growing concern across Southeast Asia.
Marcos did not elaborate on the specific provisions of the adopted principles during his remarks.
The announcement came as ASEAN and the United States sought to strengthen their partnership across various areas, including trade, investment, technology and security.
Marcos welcomed Trump’s participation in the summit, saying the US presence reaffirmed the longstanding partnership between Washington and the Southeast Asian bloc.
“Your presence confirms what we already know, that ASEAN and the United States are partners in shaping the region’s future,” Marcos said.
The Philippine president also underscored the deep ties between Manila and Washington, noting that the two countries are marking 80 years of diplomatic relations this year.
He said the relationship is anchored on shared history, values and the enduring connections between their peoples, including millions of Filipinos and Filipino-Americans.
For the Philippines, he said, the partnership with the United States extends to practically every aspect of national life.

“When I’m asked what the most important part of your relationship with the United States is, I cannot answer the question because there is no part of our lives in the Philippines that is not involved with the United States in some way, in some shape or form or another,” Marcos said.
Next year, ASEAN and the United States will mark 50 years of dialogue relations and five years of their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
Marcos said he looked forward to further strengthening the relationship between ASEAN and the United States, as well as the bilateral partnership between the Philippines and Washington.
“We look forward to celebrating all the milestones between ASEAN and the United States and the Philippines and the United States,” he said.
“We look forward to continuing to have you as our friend and as our partner," he added. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Iran dismisses report of alleged 'dirty bomb' attack on Washington
articles.summary: Iran has said CNN's claim that Tehran would attack Washington with a "dirty bomb" was an attempt to manufacture further legitimacy to continue the war. Trump has said his administration takes the…

image.caption: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei has said the report was "a malicious campaign to manufacture propaganda" [FILE: November 15, 2026]Image: Sha Dati/Xinhua/picture alliance

blocks.text: Iran on Tuesday dismissed a CNN report that Tehran was preparing a so-called "dirty bomb plot."
US President Donald Trump said his administration was taking the report "very seriously."
What did reports say about an Iranian attack on Washington?

Tehran's dismissal came after CNN reported on Tuesday that "Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials by detonating a so-called dirty bomb or a chemical weapon in Washington, DC," citing multiple US intelligence sources.

The article also reported that "US intelligence has picked up Iranian chatter claiming that it has stashed bomb-making materials inside the country" and that "many national security officials assume that pre-positioned nuclear materials have already been in the US for years," citing, again, multiple US intelligence sources.
Iran's regime: Inside the system protecting its rulers
When asked about the story during his visit to the Philippines, Trump said that if there was such a threat, Iran would "pay a price the likes of which no other country has ever paid before."
"I hope it's not, but we take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy," he added.
Iran decries 'fabrication'
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei slammed the report, calling it "a malicious campaign to manufacture propaganda."
"Those who initiated the aggression against Iran are now seeking to lay the media groundwork for their sinister designs by manufacturing and disseminating baseless allegations," he said on X.

"Step by step, they are attempting to manufacture a veneer of legitimacy for further aggression and atrocities," he said, naming CNN's reporting on the alleged "dirty bomb plot" and The New York Times without specifying any of its reporting.
Baghaei also said the US and Israel hit water storage reservoirs "during the recent acts of aggression."
Where does the Iran war stand?
The Iran war, started by the US and Israeli strikes on February 28, continues as negotiations to bring an end to the fighting stall.
Both US and Israel have been holding off from major attacks as they held elections over the last weeks.

Tehran has said it is in control the Strait of Hormuz, a key transit point for global oil and natural gas supplies, while continuing to attack ships it considers unauthorized users of the waterway. There are near-daily reports of ships hitting mines in parts of the strait Tehran says are unauthorized for transit.
The US Navy, which is enforcing its own blockade of Iranian vessels, has recently escorted tankers through the strait.
Republicans rebuke Trump on Iran war, economy after midterm wipeout
Before the midterm elections, Trump said, "We may do another little Epic Fury," referring to US-Israeli strikes that started the war, though he did not provide any timeframe.
Trump is expected to meet Chinese President ‌Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of an APEC leaders' summit in China on Thursday and discuss ending the ​war in Iran.
Pakistan-mediated peace talks between the US and Iran on April failed to reach a conclusion.
Qatar, another mediator in the war, on Tuesday called for restraint "to avoid any escalation that could undermine negotiation efforts."
Trump, Xi, Putin to hold first-ever trilateral meeting
